media: Below is a video of someone playing it: the first evening of the season in full (at one point the player zooms all the way in for a low view), then a montage of later evenings (each one shown from its opening and then from just before the sun sets), ending with the last minute of a night watch.
first_impression: Looks like an actual, genuine sheepdog sim wrapped in a lovely Scottish countryside aesthetic rather than just a meme game. The herding ring mechanic and the trial gates immediately caught my eye, though the animations look a bit stiff and low-budget.
best_things: The variety across the seasonal calendar is legit, introducing genuine herding challenges like stubborn rams, runaway lambs, dog trials, flooding streams, and thick fog.
The influence circle and creep/lie-down controls capture real-world sheepdog work better than almost any herding mechanic I've played.
The tense wolf-attack rescue mechanic with the countdown and distance tracker turns routine herding into genuine clutch moments.

worst_problems.problem: The ground-level zoomed-in camera cuts through tree geometry and feels terrible to navigate compared to the top-down view.
worst_problems.suggestion: Either fix collision/transparency on forest canopy and foliage or keep the camera strictly top-down isometric with a dynamic zoom instead of a full ground plunge.

worst_problems.problem: The HUD is crowded with explanatory helper text boxes at the bottom and center that clutter the screen during gameplay.
worst_problems.suggestion: Fade tutorial tips out after the first ten seconds and tuck control reminders into a cleaner toggleable corner widget.

worst_problems.problem: Pip and the sheep have very robotic turning and sliding motions without weight or lean, making movement feel stiff.
worst_problems.suggestion: Add proper procedural bank/lean to Pip when sprinting and soften sheep flocking physics so they don't look like sliding white blobs.

worst_problems.problem: The river bridge choke points trigger awkward clumping and glitchy shoving between sheep models.
worst_problems.suggestion: Widen bridge approach pathing or give sheep single-file queuing logic so they cross cleanly without bouncing off wooden rails.

worst_problems.problem: The sunset transition cutscene rips camera control away while you're in the middle of active herding routes.
worst_problems.suggestion: Transition the lighting and sky color seamlessly in real time during play rather than pausing for a cinematic camera pan.

boredom_points: Slow walking behind the sheep across long empty straight dirt roads when no predators or hazards are nearby (e.g. 08:20 - 08:35).
Waiting for the night watch dawn timer to tick down while standing still around a settled flock (13:15 - 13:23).
confusions: Why the low-angle zoom exists at 00:53 when all tactical information and wolf warnings happen from top-down.
How wolf aggro range is determined when they stalk from off-screen treelines.
wish_list: Whistle commands to direct second dogs or flank left/right remotely.
Endless procedural trial mode or community trial builder with custom gates and obstacles.
Cosmetic dog customization (different collie coats, bandanas, sheep breeds).
one_line_review: A surprisingly smart, authentic, and cozy sheepdog sim that nails the tension of highland herding despite stiff animations.
